paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: Illustrating the empirical generalization errors and sharpness measures with respect to QLoRA weights. (<ref>) Smaller adapters with a rank of 16 achieve the lowest generalization errors. Additionally, the Hessian trace values correlate with generalization errors, suggesting that smaller adapters tend to converge to flatter minima. (<ref>) An ensemble of k adapters leads to lower generalization errors and Hessian traces. Here, we fix the sum of the dimensions of k adapters to be equal to 256. (<ref>) QLoRA, which is trained on a quantized base model, yields lower generalization errors and Hessian trace values compared to LoRA.

model_annotations.German: This bar chart illustrates the "Error (RTE)" for two distinct methods across different rank sizes. The horizontal category axis is labeled "Rank" and displays discrete numerical categories arranged in ascending order: 4, 16, 64, and 256. The vertical value axis lacks a distinct axis label but represents the error metric indicated in the title; it features a linear scale starting at 0.3, with numeric tick marks spaced at regular intervals of 0.3 (0.3, 0.6, and 0.9). The chart uses grouped vertical bars, where each rank category contains a pair of side-by-side bars. Based on the prominently displayed legend, the blue bars represent "LoRA" (positioned on the left of each group) and the green bars represent "QLoRA" (positioned on the right). Every bar is visually emphasized with a black vertical error bar with horizontal caps centered at the top, indicating variability. Across the categories, the approximate values for the blue LoRA bars are 0.59 at rank 4, 0.61 at rank 16, 0.69 at rank 64, and reaching the tallest overall bar height of roughly 0.77 at rank 256. The green QLoRA bars have approximate values of 0.55 at rank 4, the shortest overall bar height of about 0.47 at rank 16, 0.50 at rank 64, and 0.64 at rank 256. A light gray grid spans the background of the plot area, aligning with the tick marks on both axes.
